params.method: MEASURED from assembly_valheim.dll 1.0.12. WearNTear::UpdateSupport: support(child) = max over touching neighbours of support(n)*(1 - loss*(d+0.1)), d being centre-of-mass distance, loss the child's horizontalLoss or a Lerp to verticalLoss by the support direction's angle; a piece whose collider overlaps the `terrain` layer is pinned to maxSupport. params.text: SEQ 34 IS A PHANTOM RECORD. It is mine, op zones_generate, role road_segment, and the command it describes WAS NEVER SENT. Produced by the LiveBuilder(dry=True) defect: dry mode still APPENDS its records and still runs check_expect against the LIVE server, so the record was written, nothing was sent, and the postcondition failed with zone_ctrl want 8 got 0 for zones [[-1,-1],[0,-1],[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[2,0],[2,1],[3,1]]. NOT deleted and NOT rewritten: the chain is hash-linked and an append-only log with a labelled wart is worth more than an edited one. ON REPLAY IT IS BENIGN, and the reasoning is recorded rather than assumed: zones_generate is idempotent, and on a replay the zones really are generated, so the postcondition that failed at write time PASSES at replay time. It self-heals. That is luck specific to THIS op -- a phantom objects_clear or spawn_plan would NOT self-heal. Nobody uses dry=True again; the pre-flight is `ribbon.py --validate`, which builds the records, runs schema.validate, appends nothing and touches no console.

params.text: CLEAR-RADIUS POLICY IS PER OPERATION AND BOTH BEHAVIOURS ARE CORRECT, recorded so a future reader does not see two and conclude one is a bug. Crossings CLIPS its objects_clear radius (13.1 -> 10.3 m, poi_clipped true, binding instance named) because the clear exists only to make room for a deck it has already sized, and a smaller clear still admits the structure. SettleBuild REFUSES, because a clipped radius leaves forest standing against a wall and a town pad needs its whole footprint clear. RoadNet does NEITHER: this pipeline emits NO objects_clear at all, so it has no clearing radius to bound. A road ribbon DELETES NOTHING, which is exactly the claim that earns it the non-destructive clearance budget, and it is verifiable from my own records rather than asserted.

FORDS AND CAUSEWAYS ARE TERRAIN AND THEREFORE RoadNet's; BRIDGES ARE STRUCTURES AND THEREFORE Crossings'. Boundary agreed with Crossings and recorded once. The test is MEASURED and is DEPTH, not length: ground no more than 1.0 m below the water plane (y=30.0, ZoneSystem::c_WaterLevel, a static literal float32(30.)) can be filled to road freeboard well inside the measured +/-8 m ApplyToHeightmap clamp, so it is a levelled paved causeway at ANY length; anything deeper is a bridge. The first version of this test used an 8 m LENGTH cap and it produced a 450 m 'bridge' over a tidal flat on the dock approach and turned the entire 346 m west-isle link between the two bridge abutments into a bridge -- the mirror image of planning a 12 m bridge over a 40 m river.

params.cause: Ledger._append_raw read the chain head, computed prev and wrote, with no lock and with the head CACHED at open: a lost-update race between two long-lived builders. The console token could never have prevented it, because note and observe send nothing to the console and took no token. Fixed under this record's own write path: an exclusive flock across read-head-then-write, with the head re-read from the file inside the critical section.
params.text: seq is ADVISORY from file line 47 onward -- 43-46 each appear twice. Replay, resume progress and merged_from must key on FILE POSITION, the only total order this artefact has. Nothing was renumbered and no prev was rewritten: a log edited to look clean is worth less than one carrying a labelled wart.

THE REPAIR, authorised by Main, in ledger/writer.py and ledger/schema.py only. (1) schema.scan walks the log in FILE ORDER and reports forks AS DATA; chain_head no longer raises on a prev that matches an EARLIER line's digest, and still raises on a prev that matches no line at all -- that is an edit, not a race. An integrity check whose only failure mode is total refusal cannot record its own finding, which is why a damaged log could not be annotated. Strictness for REPLAY stays in replay.py, which is BuildLedger's file: opening to append and opening to replay are different questions, and one function was answering both with the stricter answer. (2) _append_raw holds an exclusive flock across read-head-then-write and RE-READS the head from the file inside the critical section -- the re-read is the decisive half, because a lock with a cached head reproduces this fork exactly. _cross_record_checks runs inside the lock, deliberately: both guards read prior records, so the window between the read and the write is exactly where they go inert. The lock is never held across a console round trip, it carries a 30 s timeout, and it names its holder so a crash reads as 'held by pid N since T' rather than as a hang. close_report now reports every fork and every duplicate seq as a problem, and reports portal tag ends by FILE LINE as well as by seq, so an ambiguous label cannot be the only thing a reader is given.

params.method: MEASURED: the cylinder holds no clearable object, so there is nothing for `objects_remove` to do. Sending it with an empty id list would answer `Error: Missing ids.` and remove nothing, which is a silent no-op dressed as a step.

MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 47.03 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 49.87 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

piece_reach_gate.method: MEASURED: min over all instances of (distance - max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) less 1 m of slack. The clearing cylinder must not reach a location's PIECES, which is not the question the pad stand-off asks.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 48.34 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

value.why: 30 m ramp from the portal hall down onto the S2 bridge deck. The hall stands 6.8 m above the abutment 30 m away, so no 12 % profile reaches it -- interval propagation PROVED 2 stations infeasible at 12 %. The measured requirement is 22 %, which is under the network's 25 % ceiling and less than a third of the 38 deg (78 %) angle at which Character::GetSlideAngle makes a player slide. A short bridge ramp is the right answer here; a 60 m switchback to save 10 % of grade over 30 m is worse for someone on foot.

The notch depth is the applied-minus-generated height at the road stations either side of the unwritten sample, which is how far the hole's floor sits below the carriageway.

value.defect: ribbon.py::lateral_and_y REJECTED a projection parameter outside [0, 1] instead of CLAMPING it, so the wedge on the outside of every polyline vertex was claimed by no segment and its samples were never written. MEASURED: I hand-probed zone (10,-2) minutes later with `objects_count _ZoneCtrl pos=640,-128 max=1` and got 1 -- the zone had generated. BuildLedger extracted replay.verify_expect(srv, rec) and both paths now poll. The records are left in place: the chain is history, not a summary, and the successful re-emits follow them because zones_generate is idempotent.

A* simply ran the same corridor in the other direction.

value.why: building it would repaint T10's corridor 0.5 m across at full ZDO cost and add no walkable metre. The tell was that the clobber guard would have required merged_from against my own segment. Two roads half a metre apart are one road.

params.method: MEASURED: T12's terrain_write at file line 185 (seq 181) has NO save record after it -- RoadNet's run ended first -- and after SiteFinish's container restart I counted `objects_count _TerrainCompiler pos=cx,cz max=31 ignore=` at all 8 of its zone centres and got 1 at every one. So the write survived a restart it was never explicitly saved through. INFERRED, and left inferred: the flush was either the server's periodic autosave or another actor's `save`; the timestamps could distinguish them and nobody has measured it.

value.what_it_means: a missing save record does NOT imply the work was lost, and a save record does NOT make terrain durable. Neither direction may be inferred from its presence.

value.why: 30 m ramp from the portal hall down onto the S2 bridge deck. The hall stands 6.8 m above the abutment 30 m away, so no 12 % profile reaches it -- interval propagation PROVED 2 stations infeasible at 12 %. The measured requirement is 22 %, which is under the network's 25 % ceiling and less than a third of the 38 deg (78 %) angle at which Character::GetSlideAngle makes a player slide. A short bridge ramp is the right answer here; a 60 m switchback to save 10 % of grade over 30 m is worse for someone on foot.

The radius is now snapped to the MIDPOINT of a gap between rings and REFUSES when no gap containing a piece fits. Under the fix this unit's radius is 2.49 m with 28 of 28 rows inside, which is the check that should have run. NOT RE-EMITTED: re-sending would stand a second hut.

params.method: MEASURED per PIECE, not per disc. Piece positions come from each protected structure's OWN spawn_plan blob in the blob store -- the literal command list it was built from -- with field order pos=<z>,<x>,<y>, confirmed against three structures whose expect.prefab_count positions are (x,z) and whose counts verified live. The applied height change at each piece is ribbon.delta_at, the bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around it with unwritten samples contributing zero, which is how Heightmap renders ground -- so an untouched piece reads exactly 0.0. Over-water is generated height below the MEASURED c_WaterLevel of 30.0. This is the state BEFORE the protected-piece keep-out was added to the rasteriser; after it, every one of these reads 0.0 by construction, because the keep-out excludes exactly the samples that can contribute to a piece's blend (Chebyshev <= 1.0 m).

value.why: 30 m ramp from the portal hall down onto the S2 bridge deck. The hall stands 6.8 m above the abutment 30 m away, so no 12 % profile reaches it -- interval propagation PROVED 2 stations infeasible at 12 %. The measured requirement is 22 %, which is under the network's 25 % ceiling and less than a third of the 38 deg (78 %) angle at which Character::GetSlideAngle makes a player slide. A short bridge ramp is the right answer here; a 60 m switchback to save 10 % of grade over 30 m is worse for someone on foot.

params.text: SEGMENTS DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT, with the measured reason, because the world cannot record what was not done. (1) T11-wtsouth-wtspawn is T10 reversed: 286 nodes against 286, endpoints swapped, worst lateral offset 0.537 m, identical zone set - building it would repaint T10 at full ZDO cost and add no walkable metre (observe T11_is_T10_reversed_not_a_second_road). (2) S13-stathub-dock and S14-eastlobe-ferryeast validate clean but TERMINATE AT dock-stationhub and ferry-terminal-east, both of which have zero pieces in the world (measured above). A road to nothing is worse than no road; build the structures first, then these. (3) T1-portalhub-temple and S1-portalhub-brgs2 are VALIDATED AND REFUSED, not abandoned: both write into zone (-5,3), which holds the spawn portal ring's seq 170 - a zones_generate carrying flatten=FORBIDDEN with site_id 'portal-ring', no pieces and no disc. The ring's four portals ARE recorded (file lines 175, 176, 191, 194) but under role 'spawn_portal' with no site_id, so the site-grouped piece lookup does not join them to seq 170 and the guard correctly fails closed. Declaring site_id 'portal-ring' on those portal records, or recording the ring's extent, unblocks both. T1 measures 5,127 samples over 10 zones, clearance clear, delta gate 0.000 m, 0 past the clamp, 1542/1542 centreline stations on road, WALKABLE at 0.1026 over 8 m. S1 measures 215 samples over 2 zones, 22 skipped beside bridge-s2 pieces so every piece reads 0.000 m, WALKABLE at 0.2502 over 8 m, and its ramp reaches exactly 30.600 m - the abutment level Crossings and RoadNet agreed - against deck floor pieces at 30.503, with 1.5 m of untouched ground between them standing at 30.97 to 31.05, i.e. a natural hump 0.37-0.44 m high and then a step down onto the deck. Walkable, and measured rather than assumed. (4) S7-stathub-wtnorth was refused for dock-stationhub and is built above once its census landed.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

piece_reach_gate.method: MEASURED: min over all instances of (distance - max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) less 1 m of slack. The clearing cylinder must not reach a location's PIECES, which is not the question the pad stand-off asks.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 40.45 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrives between the measurement and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the command.

piece_reach_gate.method: MEASURED: min over all instances of (distance - max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) less 1 m of slack. The clearing cylinder must not reach a location's PIECES, which is not the question the pad stand-off asks.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 33.12 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this pipeline emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. value.why: 30 m ramp from the portal hall down onto the S2 bridge deck. The hall stands 6.8 m above the abutment 30 m away, so no 12 % profile reaches it -- interval propagation PROVED 2 stations infeasible at 12 %. The measured requirement is 22 %, which is under the network's 25 % ceiling and less than a third of the 38 deg (78 %) angle at which Character::GetSlideAngle makes a player slide. A short bridge ramp is the right answer here; a 60 m switchback to save 10 % of grade over 30 m is worse for someone on foot.

The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 35.4 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

value.cause: `zone_list` named every zone the pad's BOUNDING SQUARE touches, while `clear.generate_max` reaches radius+45.25 m, which is exactly the set the DISC touches. Zone (-15,27)'s centre is 56.00 m from the cylinder centre against a generate_max of 55.77, so UpgradeWorld correctly did not generate it and the gate correctly refused the four it had been told to expect. The disc's own x extent at that zone's z bound 1760.0 is [-927.36,-909.44] and the zone edge is at -928.00, so the cylinder never enters it.
value.fix: tools/jumpstart/settlements/build.py::zone_list now tests each candidate zone's 64 m square against the disc and keeps only the ones it actually intersects. REGRESSION CHECKED on every unit built tonight: wt-spawn, wt-south, wt-town, lh-south and the three remaining vestvik units all have worst zone-centre distance inside their own generate_max.

value.verdict: FALSE NEGATIVE -- the world is correct, the gate's zone list was not

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED live over RCON: every `portal_wood` inside 30 m of the castle and 40 m of each village centre, listed with its tag.

value.impact_on_this_project: NONE of the 17 is one of ours and none of our tags is affected: every tag this project placed has EXACTLY two ends, read back off the ZDO. The hazard is that the operator cannot tell one of these arches from ours by looking -- and at vestvik the pre-existing untagged arch stands 5.91 m from our own u-vestvik site end.
value.measured_by: findObjects -prefab portal_wood -detailed via replay.bounded_detailed, deduplicated by ZDO id
value.mechanism: Valheim pairs portals BY TAG and the default tag is the empty string, so every one of these 17 shares one tag. They form a single random pool: stepping into any of them delivers the operator to an arbitrary other one, including 920 m away at the other village. `TeleportWorld::GetHoverText` shows the tag only inside `m_maxInteractDistance` 5.0 m and an empty tag shows nothing, so there is no warning at the arch.
value.not_done: not re-tagged and not deleted. Deleting them is the unrepairable damage class for the two mod-village ones, and the castle's fifteen are pieces of the body the plan asked for. Re-tagging would need a ZDO field write, which is not an op this ledger has, and inventing one to tidy decor is a worse trade than reporting it.

The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

piece_reach_gate.method: MEASURED: min over all instances of (distance - max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) less 1 m of slack. The clearing cylinder must not reach a location's PIECES, which is not the question the pad stand-off asks.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 32.42 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

piece_reach_gate.method: MEASURED: min over all instances of (distance - max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM)) less 1 m of slack. The clearing cylinder must not reach a location's PIECES, which is not the question the pad stand-off asks.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 55.33 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

params.method: MEASURED: earlier per-zone TCData blobs re-read from the ledger's blob store and unioned per SAMPLE INDEX, ours winning only where we wrote. `compiler_present` is a live `objects_count _TerrainCompiler` at the zone centre, because a record is appended BEFORE it is sent and an append whose send failed leaves a claim with no compiler behind it -- which is the case for this build's own first attempt at stenvik-hall-1.

meta.why: one compiler per zone, deleted before spawn so the op is idempotent; the pad is levelled per BUILDING because MEASURED no 176 m district on this seed can be written inside TerrainComp's +/-8 m clamp

params.datum: pad target_y 75.7 m from plan.json, deltas against patchscan generated heights at 1 m (seed Pirate68)

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

meta.policy: REFUSE, never clip: a town pad needs its WHOLE footprint clear or the building stands in trees. Crossings clips because a smaller clear still admits an already-sized deck. Two operations, two policies, one reason each.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every instance within 60 m of the written samples, the APPLIED height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's OWN measured reach disc by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders ground. Probing the DISC rather than the marker matters: a location's pieces are spread over its reach and the marker can be metres from the piece that would float.

Its postcondition was never measured: the wire's trailing literal `start` hit a finished operation, ValheimRcon answered 'routine is null', and `console_echo` refused the reply. Both faults are now refused by the schema: a `zones_restore` or an `empty` `zones_generate` carrying a literal `start` line is rejected at write time, because `send_wire` already brackets a staged verb with stop/cmd/start. seq 741 stands as a failed attempt, which is what it was.

params.method:
MEASURED, and it SUPERSEDES the cause in seq 738 while confirming every symptom there. The zone is NOT phantom-generated: it is genuinely UNGENERATED and `SpawnZone` refuses it. Evidence, four independent readings plus the IL:
(1) `ZoneSystem::SpawnZone` (IL of the deployed assembly_valheim.dll, method at RVA 0xbc404) has exactly TWO `return false` paths: IL_0030-003b, terrain not ready; and IL_003c-0067, `m_locationInstances.TryGetValue(zoneID, out li) && !li.m_placed && !PokeCanSpawnLocation(li.m_location, true)`. `PokeCanSpawnLocation` returns `LocationPrefabLoadData.IsLoaded` for the location's SoftReference prefab -- a per-LOCATION-TYPE async asset load, not a per-instance property.
(2) `locations_list * pos=2368,-3328 max=45` answers exactly one row: `MountainCave02: (2368, -3328, 131) Mountain` -- an UNPLACED location registration sitting on the zone centre. 118 MountainCave02 registrations exist world-wide (`locations_count`).
(3) Upgrade World's completion lines, read from the container log rather than from the init string: the site-wide run said 'Generate completed. 3 zones generated. 1 errors.' and the scoped run said 'Generate completed. 0 zones generated. 1 errors.' -- `ZoneOperation::MoveToNextZone` only counts an error after TEN SECONDS of `ExecuteZone` returning false, so this is ~600 consecutive false returns, twice, five minutes apart. A heightmap build resolves in milliseconds and (36,-52) generated afterwards, so path (1)-terrain is excluded and path (1)-location is what refuses.
(4) `zones_restore pos=2368,-3328 max=1` answers '0 zones: 448 skipped by the command'. `RestoreZones` sets TargetZones=Generated, so its candidate set IS the save's generated set (448 zones) -- and this zone is not in it. `zones_generate` sets TargetZones=Ungenerated and selects it ('1 zones'). The two commands' target sets are disjoint and both agree the zone is ungenerated.

params.text: FIXTURE AUDIT for sudrberg-keep is NOT clean, and the reason is the BODY, not the pad. MEASURED: 104 carried fixtures, 85 pierce failures, 2 preference failures, 1 portal failure. The pierces are the blueprint's own geometry -- 51 of 68 itemstands penetrate the stone_pillar or blackmarble_base_1 they are MOUNTED ON by a median 0.09 m, 3 signs likewise at 0.09 m, 29 black-metal chests sit 0.13-0.52 m into the walls they back onto, and the body's own carried portal_wood is 0.30 m into a wood_pole. The hearth at (2405.80, 122.24, -3353.32) wants indoor_covered and classifies `blocked` because it is set 0.58 m into a blackmarble_2x1x1 -- but it is measurably UNDER COVER and INDOOR: six of the body's own solids stand in the column directly above it, the lowest a wood_wall_log floor 8.90 m up and the highest at y=140.24 (about 18 m of building overhead), its wall gap is 4.935 m, and the body offers 54 m2 of indoor-covered interior. This body carries NO BED (plan `beds: 0`), so there is no bed to be in the rain. The same audit shape is on the sibling castle: hognest-castle reports clean=false with 15 failures over 16 carried fixtures, all of them its own portals inside its own pillars. Making this clean means editing the blueprint body, which would make this keep different from the fourteen sites already standing -- so it is REPORTED, not quietly fixed, and not claimed as clean.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY: `findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r` per prefab per tile, subdivided with overlapping quadrants until every reply is under 18 rows, deduplicated by ZDO id, and re-filtered in XZ because findObjects takes a CUBE while objects_count takes a CYLINDER. No objects_count is used here at all -- its table goes through the container console sink, which failed three times in this session and which this census in its first form is what killed. The prefab NAMES come from corridor_prefabs.json, the one set of `objects_count id=*` tables taken before that outage; a name missing from it can be MISSED but never deleted, because the wire's `ids` are built from the per-cylinder census taken at removal time. Lateral distance is ribbon.lateral_and_y against this segment's own polyline, i.e. the same function that decided where the road went.

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

params.method: MEASURED: A* over a 1 m PatchScan field (rivers included) with the achievable surface clipped to +/-7 m of generated ground; profile fitted by exact interval propagation under the grade limit and the cut/fill box

meta.why: paint alpha is NOT honoured on a zone that has never been generated -- MEASURED, a paved_cleared pad in an ungenerated zone still planted 30+ vegetation ZDOs up to 7.68 m above it

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T12_wtspawn_temple

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY: `findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r` per prefab per tile, subdivided with overlapping quadrants until every reply is under 18 rows, deduplicated by ZDO id, and re-filtered in XZ because findObjects takes a CUBE while objects_count takes a CYLINDER. No objects_count is used here at all -- its table goes through the container console sink, which failed three times in this session and which this census in its first form is what killed. The prefab NAMES come from corridor_prefabs.json, the one set of `objects_count id=*` tables taken before that outage; a name missing from it can be MISSED but never deleted, because the wire's `ids` are built from the per-cylinder census taken at removal time. Lateral distance is ribbon.lateral_and_y against this segment's own polyline, i.e. the same function that decided where the road went.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.text: ANNOTATION OF seq 933, which is NOT edited and must not be. That record is an observe of road_surface_clearing_plan appended under actor RoadClear. RoadClear had already yielded; the record was written by RoadEmit running clear.py emit --dry solely to find out whether the DESTRUCTIVE POI gate would refuse T12, and LiveBuilder(dry=True) appended anyway. Two defects, both now fixed in this session: dry=True built and appended instead of building and validating (fixed - Ledger.build returns the record a call to append WOULD write, schema-validated, unwritten and unsent), and the actor came from a module-level constant rather than from the caller (fixed - clear.py ACTOR is RoadEmit and LiveBuilder refuses an empty actor). Read seq 933 as: measured by RoadEmit, tool tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census, artefact /tmp/roads/clear/T12.json, and not as an action RoadClear took. The real T12 clearing is seq 951-963 with save 964.

params.method: MEASURED live, PER CELL rather than per station. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 32 m cells on a global 32 m lattice aligned with the zone grid, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell: one `objects_count id=* ignore=_* max=22.63` names every prefab present in the cylinder that CONTAINS the cell -- strictly more complete than corridor_prefabs.json's 139 names, which cannot see a mod POI -- then `findObjects -prefab P -near cx y cz 16` per named prefab at THREE y levels (-32, 0, +32), because the wire takes one radius for all three axes and a single box would truncate everything more than 16 m above the road: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall for exactly that reason. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin -- not the old 1.4143 half-diagonal, which covered 2.8x the volume and reached into the neighbouring cell). Deduplicated by ZDO id. Because the cells and the y levels are disjoint, each object is echoed to the container log ONCE instead of the ~10 times the overlapping per-station discs cost. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.text: AGENT HANDOFF, recorded because the actor field cannot carry it: seq 1006 onward of this road-repair pass are emitted by RoadFinish, continuing RoadEmit's pass (T12 seq 951-968, T3 seq 970-1003) under the same actor name so a segment is not split across two labels. RoadFinish also replaced the per-station corridor census with a per-cell one (clear.py::census_zoned): disjoint 32 m cells on the zone-aligned lattice, prefab names measured per cell by objects_count id=*, three y levels per cell because findObjects -near is a CUBE in Y as well -- the old per-station discs were blind to everything more than a disc radius above the road, MEASURED at the T10 spawn hall (six wood_beam_1 at y 84-85 invisible to a 7.42 m box centred at 75.73). Proven against a per-station run over the same sub-range of T10: identical ZDO id sets (189 objects, 0 either way), 588 socket calls / 994 echoed lines per-station vs 248 + 3 console / 794 + 67 per-cell. Full T10: 1099 socket + 22 console calls, 2948 + 351 echoed lines, 1395 objects.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

params.text: ANNOTATION OF seq 1054 AND seq 1136, neither of which is edited. T4-meadhall-stathub clearing, by RoadFinish. seq 1054: the record was appended and its WIRE WAS NEVER SENT -- replay._staged raised OutputNotFound on console("stop") because the container log chain had stalled, so nothing was removed under that seq. Its cylinder (304.0,386.0) was re-emitted and CONFIRMED under seq 1056. seq 1136: appended for cylinder 86 of 95 and its effect is UNKNOWN -- the RCON socket was refused mid-op because something outside this session sent SIGTERM to the container at 09:27:59 (supervisord logged a clean shutdown, valheim-server exit status 0, and an external process then recreated the container). CONFIRMED on T4: cylinders 1..85 of 95, 80 objects_clear records with verified postconditions (objects_count total 0), 764 objects removed, seq 1056-1135. FIVE cylinders skipped at emit by the live per-cylinder census: (496,462) Pickable_SurtlingCoreStand; (504,470) a forest crypt (TreasureChest_forestcrypt, Pickable_ForestCryptRandom/Remains04, 6x SurtlingCoreStand, root07); (575,751), (501,843) and (550,922) had nothing left to remove. SEVENTEEN more were skipped at plan time by a blocker inside the disc. NOT DONE on T4: cylinders 86..95, and the battered terrain repair of seq 213 -- so T4 is a PARTIALLY CLEARED road with its ORIGINAL unbattered earthwork. Its before-census baseline and placed-object set must be re-derived after the remaining cylinders land, because placed_after is the census minus the VERIFIED removals and that set changed. The world was saved after the removals and they are verified persistent: findObjects at (580,990) and (304,386) answer No objects found after the shutdown. TRANSPORT REPAIRS made in this pass, all measured: (1) the corridor census is socket-only and uses UNSCOPED findObjects -near per 16 m cell (rcon.guard now permits the unscoped form inside 8 m, which is where the reply stays ~5 KB at the densest corridor density measured) -- no prefab list and no console at all; (2) console.py reads the console output from the container own file /var/log/supervisor/valheim-server-stdout---*.log from a byte offset taken before the command, because docker logs stopped carrying anything twice while that file kept growing; (3) rcon.host_sink_state/drain_log_sink_host/keep_sink_clear read and repair the sink from the HOST, and console.run_console now drains before re-reading a missing echo; (4) replay._staged sends stop/start as plain socket round trips and records the reply, because consoleCommand start answers routine is null rather than the stock echo, so console_echo refuses a command that ran.

AGENT HANDOFF, recorded because the actor field cannot carry it: from this record on, the Ulfsland road repair is run by RoadLast, continuing RoadFinish's pass (T4 clearing seq 1056-1136) which continued RoadEmit's (T12 seq 951-968, T3 seq 970-1003, T10 seq 1006-1051). Unlike its predecessors this agent records its OWN name: `ribbon.py` and `clear.py` now take --actor and REQUIRE it, because the module constant they defaulted to is also the PatchScan sandbox name and the two are different questions. TOKEN TAKEN. World backed up to /media/big4/projects/game/valheim/world_backups/world-Ulfsland-backup-2026-09-16_09-38-32.tgz before the first write.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON socket, in one call, on each record's OWN cylinder: `objects_count` scoped to exactly the prefab names on that record's wire over exactly that centre and radius, PLUS an unscoped `objects_count id=*` over the same cylinder as a cross-check that the scoped answer is not a filter artefact. A removal's effect is the absence of the things it named from the place it named, so that is what was asked. Nothing here is inferred from the transcript of the run that died.

params.text:
RESOLUTION OF seq 1054 AND seq 1136, BY MEASUREMENT. Neither record is edited; seq 1137 annotated them as unfulfilled and this append annotates them again with the live answer.
seq 1054 -- cylinder (304.0, 386.0) r 7.01, ids Pickable_Dandelion, Pickable_Stone, Rock_3. MEASURED NOW: 0 objects, scoped and unscoped. The cylinder is clear. WHICH record cleared it is not decidable by census, because seq 1054 and seq 1056 carry byte-identical wires -- but it IS decided by seq 1056's own in-call live census, which is a measurement and not a transcript: `deleted_live_count: 4` means `objects_count id=*` found all four objects STILL STANDING immediately before seq 1056 sent, AFTER seq 1054 had been appended. So seq 1054 HAD NO EFFECT and seq 1056 is the record that removed them. VERDICT: seq 1054 unfulfilled, effect nil, superseded and fulfilled by seq 1056.
seq 1136 -- cylinder (583.38, 994.44) r 7.45, ids Beech1, Beech_small1, Pickable_Dandelion, Rock_4. MEASURED NOW: 4 objects, one of each named prefab, scoped total 4 and unscoped total 4. These are cylinder 86 of 95 and they are the objects seq 1136 named: Beech1 65928:1 at (589.18, 995.42), Beech_small1 65971:1 at (590.11, 994.49), Pickable_Dandelion 66008:1 at (577.01, 997.52), Rock_4 65899:1 at (588.72, 994.52). VERDICT: seq 1136 HAD NO EFFECT. Either its wire never reached the socket or its effect was lost with the container SIGTERM at 09:27:59 before any save. The cylinder is re-emitted in this pass and its removal is verified by a NEW record rather than credited to seq 1136.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BATTER, and this is why the question had to be asked before the terrain write: the batter's placed-object gate is the census MINUS the verified removals. Crediting seq 1136 would have told the batter that a standing Beech1 5.76 m off the centreline was gone, and the batter would have re-graded the ground out from under it -- the floating-tree defect this whole pass repairs, recreated by the repair. seq 1136 is therefore EXCLUDED from the verified-removal set until a new record proves that cylinder empty.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.
