delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T4_meadhall_stathub

params.method: MEASURED off the LIVE BLOBS with tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py both times: every terrain_write blob for T4's 21 zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER, added to the cached PatchScan generated heights and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. The BEFORE run is seq 1158's own `repair_before` baseline, taken before the write; the AFTER run is the same instrument on the same zones afterwards. The verdict limit is BATTER_GRADE 0.7813 plus the segment's own 0.08 longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance = 0.8613 m per metre.

carriageway_step_max.owner: stenvik-beehive-1#286, a site_pad: the 89 m clobber, which the PAD wins

params.method: MEASURED on segments.yaml's own node list: every pair of centreline nodes at least six nodes apart whose plan distance is within 8.0 m -- the full written carriageway width, 6 m paved plus 1 m of shoulder each side -- reported with the difference between their FITTED PROFILE HEIGHTS. Two legs of one road closer than its own width write the same lattice samples at two different design heights, and last-writer-wins per sample turns that difference into a 1 m transverse step that no batter can remove, because both sides of it are carriageway. Cross-checked against the applied surface: each residual step was re-measured on the GENERATED ground at the same two points, so a hillside is not charged to this write.
params.tool: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py + a node-pair sweep over segments.yaml

params.text:
T4-meadhall-stathub BATTERED at seq 1158, a repair of seq 213, and what is left is RECORDED rather than claimed clear. By RoadLast.
WHAT MOVED, off applied.py: carriageway 1 m step p50 0.441 -> 0.221; earthwork p95 1.570 -> 1.049, max 7.988 -> 6.774; over-grade fraction 0.1151 -> 0.0676; the legacy 1 m band p50 1.036 -> 0.781, which is the design grade itself. 2,670 batter samples over 1,352 rays, 1,092 of which MET NATURAL GROUND. zone_ctrl 1 of 1 in all 21 zones, 0 samples past the +/-8 m clamp, 0 below the 30.0 m water plane.
THE 89 CLOBBERED METRES: the approach grading claimed 268 stations (217 by a foreign write, 51 by a pad stand-off) owned by stenvik-beehive-1#286, stenvik-hut-3#311 and tree-sth-1/2/3, regraded 72 profile nodes by up to 5.425 m, and took the step INTO the claim from 6.391 m to 2.642 m. Inside the pad the PAD still wins: the carriageway's worst remaining 1 m step, 6.556 m at (598.1, 966.0), is on samples seq 286 owns, and the road may not take them back.
THE 333 UNWRITTEN METRES, now 376.7 m in five runs and every one of them has a measured cause rather than being a hole: 207.2 m from (539.8, 814.2) and 69.7 m from (551.4, 930.0) terminate on stenvik's levelled pad with residual steps of -10.414 m and -2.770 m against its 45.57 m datum; 8.9 m and 43.9 m are BRIDGE, the deck being Crossings'; and 47.0 m from (479.3, 445.3) is FOREIGN_CLAIM -- MEASURED: all 1,126 written samples in zone (8,7) belong to tree-sth-2 seq 669, a site_pad, and the road's centreline runs through them for 47 m while sitting OUTSIDE every pad circle in sites.yaml. `walkability` called that a HOLE and refused the segment until it was taught to read the rasteriser's own recorded refusals instead of re-deriving them from radii -- ownership comes from the blobs, which is the same ruling that found the clobber.
WHAT IS STILL OVER GRADE, AND WHY IT IS NOT A NEW CLIFF: 33 of 6,879 earthwork pairs (0.48 %), of which 5 are steps the GENERATED ground already has at the same two points and 28 are this write's. The largest run at one lateral is 4, at (518.8-520.4, 640.0-641.8). The adjacency test had to be corrected twice before it could say that: it clustered on the CENSUS STATION CENTRE, where two steps 19 m apart across a doubled-back ribbon read as distance 0 and gave a run of 8, and it counted natural hillside as this write's work.
THE CAUSE IS THE ROUTE, NOT THE BATTER, and it is MEASURED: 859 pairs of T4's own centreline nodes at least six nodes apart lie within 8.0 m of each other -- inside the road's own written width -- with fitted profile heights differing by up to 1.254 m. A* built a switchback staircase to hold the 8 % grade on that hillside, so T4 crosses its own footprint at two design heights and last-writer-wins per sample leaves a 1 m step between two pieces of the same road. No batter can grade that: both sides of the step are carriageway. It has been there since seq 213 and removing it is a RE-ROUTE of T4, which changes where the road goes and is not this repair's to decide.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T8_stenvik_wttown

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T9_wttown_dockshore

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T5_temple_dockshore

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

location_gate.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction, so it cannot see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. Clearing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT -- the sufficient check is the live per-cylinder census, which sees a mod house's pieces as pieces and skips the cylinder.

meta.width_method: carriageway half+shoulder+1.0 m measured terrain spread, OR the batter's own taper run for the cut at that station; see clear.py docstring

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

params.method: MEASURED: A* over a 1 m PatchScan field (rivers included) with the achievable surface clipped to +/-7 m of generated ground; profile fitted by exact interval propagation under the grade limit and the cut/fill box

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_S8_wtsouth_treesth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

meta.census_timing: MEASURED in this same call, immediately before the removal -- a census taken minutes earlier is a census of a different world

cylinder.transient_why: mobile creatures, recorded and NOT counted as blockers: a prefab-scoped removal that does not name them cannot touch them and their position is gone by the next frame. MEASURED on T12: one Boar per cylinder would otherwise have left 37 trees standing in the carriageway

meta.deleted_positions_from: tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py::census -- findObjects -prefab P -near x y z r, deduplicated by ZDO id. RECORDED SO THE DELETION IS REVERSIBLE: prefab + world position + ZDO id per object. The live count in the same call is authoritative for HOW MANY; this list is authoritative for WHERE.
meta.ids_scoped_why: id=* would also delete anything that arrived between the census and the removal, and it is the command that deleted POI content in the pre-wipe world. Naming the measured prefabs makes the safety a property of the COMMAND.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_S7_stathub_wtnorth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

fords.measured: generated heights from PatchScan at 1 m, seed Pirate68

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_W5_brgs1_wsouth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED: A* over a 1 m PatchScan field (rivers included) with the achievable surface clipped to +/-7 m of generated ground; profile fitted by exact interval propagation under the grade limit and the cut/fill box

fords.built_as: levelled paved causeway at road freeboard; TERRAIN, no structure
fords.measured: generated heights from PatchScan at 1 m, seed Pirate68

value.why: the harbour on the temple's own south shore; trunk because its deck is 6 m

meta.why: paint alpha is NOT honoured on a zone that has never been generated -- MEASURED, a paved_cleared pad in an ungenerated zone still planted 30+ vegetation ZDOs up to 7.68 m above it

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.name: road_T13_temple_harboursouth

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. value.why: 36 m from the S1 east abutment, so almost free off the same trunk

meta.why: paint alpha is NOT honoured on a zone that has never been generated -- MEASURED, a paved_cleared pad in an ungenerated zone still planted 30+ vegetation ZDOs up to 7.68 m above it

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

meta.why: roads are terrain, not pieces: piece_pavedroad has no persistent ZNetView and zero road pieces exist in any fleet save

params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON socket on seq 1619's OWN cylinder: `objects_count` scoped to exactly the prefab names on its wire over exactly that centre and radius, plus an unscoped `objects_count id=*` over the same cylinder as a cross-check. seq 1619 was appended and the RCON stream closed mid-packet before its reply, so whether its removal landed is a question about the world and not about the transcript.

params.text:
ANNOTATION OF seq 1619, which is NOT edited. T1-portalhub-temple clearing, by RoadLast. The record was appended and the RCON stream closed mid-packet during its round trip. MEASURED NOW on its cylinder (-188.0, 33.66) r 7.81: scoped total 12, unscoped total 12 {'Beech_small1': 2, 'Beech_small2': 3, 'Beech1': 2, 'Pickable_Branch': 1, 'Pickable_Stone': 1, 'Rock_3': 1, 'Rock_4': 2}. VERDICT: the cylinder still holds objects seq 1619 named, so it HAD NO EFFECT and must be re-emitted; it is excluded from the verified removal set until a new record proves the cylinder empty.
T1-portalhub-temple IS PART DONE AND IS NOT BATTERED. Its per-cell census COMPLETED -- 85 of 85 cells, 3,888 objects, 1,585 socket calls -- and it took two transport fixes to get there, both now in clear.py: a box that does NOT ANSWER is subdivided into its eight tiling children rather than refused (the portal hall cells at (-296, 216) and (-280, 216) never answer as a single 8 m box because the reply exceeds the 4,050-byte cap), and a stream closed mid-packet is retried on a fresh connection like a timeout. Clearing then emitted 29 cylinders of 47 (seq 1591-1619) before the stream closed again. THE REMAINING WORK ON T1 IS: cylinders 30-47 of its clearing, then the batter as a repair of its own latest terrain_write. Its census is on disk at /tmp/roadlast/T1_census.json and is re-usable; the clearing emit is idempotent per cylinder because each one is re-censused live immediately before its removal, so re-running it completes the pass rather than repeating it. S1-portalhub-brgs2, the 30.6 m ramp onto the bridge deck, was NOT REACHED AT ALL.

params.method: MEASURED off the LIVE BLOBS before and after, with tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for this segment's zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the single per-zone compiler holds), added to the cached PatchScan generated heights at 1 m and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh -- the surface a player stands on. Transverse steps come from ribbon.py::edge_step_census, which classifies each adjacent 1 m pair as carriageway, MY EARTHWORK (the verdict), another claim's junction, or natural ground, and judges only the earthwork -- against BATTER_GRADE 0.7813 plus this segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance. The replay that produces the clip list reads OWNERSHIP with this segment's own writes removed, because the union copies every prior claim into the road's own blob and `foreign_at` would otherwise be blind to the pads the write refused. Longitudinal gradient is over an 8 m baseline with the 1 m figure beside it as a DIFFERENT quantity.

terminates_at.why: the road surface at the pad boundary against the height Settlements levels that pad to. Positive means the pad floor stands ABOVE the road and the operator has to climb it; a step over ~0.5 m cannot be walked up.

Both stopped on the same transport limit at the portal hall, which holds the densest boxes in the world: `rcon connection closed mid-packet`. seq 1619's wire is UNFULFILLED and MEASURED nil -- 12 objects still standing in its cylinder -- annotated at seq 1620/1621 and 1623/1624 and excluded from the verified removal set.
FOUR DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED IN THE INSTRUMENTS, all in tools/jumpstart/roads/: (1) `walkability` called a 47 m stretch of T4 a HOLE and refused the segment, because it re-derived the rasteriser's refusals from pad CIRCLES while the ground there is tree-sth-2 seq 669's WRITTEN footprint -- it now reads `stamp`'s own recorded refusals, which is where ownership actually lives. (2) A carriageway refusal recorded a counter and no POSITION, so the report could not say where the road stops; `road_clip_at` now records every one. (3) A ray skipped for having no written road left a wall with no trace; `ray_skip_at` now records every sample of it. (4) The over-grade census recorded the STATION CENTRE as a step's position, so an adjacency test read a doubled-back ribbon's cross section as a cliff -- it now records `step_xz` and the two samples the step is between, so a consumer can re-measure the same step on the GENERATED surface and find out whether this write made it or the hillside did.
AND ONE HAZARD THAT OUTLIVES THIS PASS, MEASURED AND NOT FIXED. THE UNION LAUNDERS FOREIGN OWNERSHIP. A repair must union every prior claim in a zone forward into its own blob, or `deleteObjects -zone` destroys them -- but the blob carries `role: road_segment` under the ROAD's name, so after the repair a site pad's samples read as the road's. MEASURED on T8: its write refused 123 carriageway samples because `foreign_at` found a pad owning them, and the identical rasterisation run against the surface that write produced finds ZERO and would pave into the pad. `foreign_at` is the instrument that implements 'inside a settlement pad the pad wins' and it is deliberately blind to radii because that is what caught T4's clobber; the union blinds it to the blobs as well. THE NEXT AGENT TO RE-REPAIR AN ALREADY-REPAIRED SEGMENT MUST REWIND OWNERSHIP PAST THAT SEGMENT'S OWN WRITES, as the verifier in /tmp/roadlast/verify_segment.py now does, or it will grade a building's foundation. The durable fix is provenance -- record which sample indices a write's own rasteriser produced, per entry -- and that is a ledger SCHEMA change, so it is the operator's call and not mine.
T4'S RESIDUAL IS THE ROUTE, NOT THE BATTER: 859 pairs of its own centreline nodes at least six nodes apart lie within its 8 m written width, 593 of them more than 0.5 m apart in fitted profile height, worst -3.583 m at (585.3, 954.0)/(592.3, 957.7) -- which is where its worst carriageway step and its 0.8849 longitudinal gradient are. A* built a switchback staircase to hold 8 % on that hillside, so T4 crosses its own footprint at two design heights and no side slope can grade a step whose both sides are carriageway. T13 has 534 such pairs, T9 208, T5 203. Removing them is a RE-ROUTE and not this repair's to decide.

params.text:
PROPOSAL, NOT APPLIED: SEPARATE WHAT THE WORLD MUST HOLD FROM WHAT A CLAIM AUTHORED. Main's ruling part 3, written up with its migration path and deliberately NOT migrated tonight.
THE DEFECT, RESTATED AS A PROPERTY RATHER THAN AN INCIDENT. A zone holds exactly one `_TerrainCompiler` and `terrain_write` does `deleteObjects -zone` before it spawns, so the blob a claim SENDS must be the union of every delta that zone must keep. The record then stores that same blob, so the ledger says this claim authored samples it merely carried. `role` and `name` come from the RECORD, so a pad's floor inside a road's blob reads as `role: road_segment` under the road's name. The blob is correct for the game and wrong for the log, and provenance is destroyed BY CONSTRUCTION -- no amount of care at write time can recover it afterwards.
THE SHAPE. Keep sending the union; stop RECORDING it. Per zone entry, record only the sample indices this claim's own rasteriser authored -- `authored_blob_sha256` plus the existing `merged_from` naming the priors by seq AND file line -- and have replay recompose the union at READ time by decoding `merged_from` in file order and overlaying the authored set. The wire is unchanged, the bytes the game receives are unchanged, and `applied.py` composes exactly what it composes today because it already unions in file order. What changes is that `foreign_at` can ask 'whose sample is this at all' and get the truth without any caller having to rewind anything.
WHY `merged_from` IS NOT ALREADY ENOUGH. It names the priors but not WHICH SAMPLES came from them, so the only way to subtract them is to re-decode every prior and assume any sample they hold was carried -- which is wrong exactly where both claims wrote the same index, and that is the contested set the ruling is about.
MIGRATION PATH, and the first step is the one that makes the rest optional. (a) NEW RECORDS FIRST: add the authored blob and keep writing the union blob beside it for one generation, so a replay can be proven byte-identical from either. (b) PROVE IT on a zone with five priors -- zone (9,15) carries seq 121, 136, 213, 218, 286 -- by recomposing and comparing sha256 against the union blob already stored. (c) EXISTING RECORDS ARE NOT REWRITTEN: the chain is append-only and `merged_from` already names each entry's priors, so the authored set for a historical entry is derivable ONLY where the priors and the entry disagree; where they agree it is genuinely unknown and must be recorded as unknown rather than guessed. Emit that as a one-off `observe` per legacy entry, not as an edit. (d) Until (a) ships, the two immediate rules below are the whole defence.
RULE 1 AND RULE 2 ARE APPLIED AND LIVE IN tools/jumpstart/roads/. Rule 1: `ribbon.py build` now drops THIS segment's own terrain_write entries from the ownership view before rasterising, so a pad's samples are inherited from the PAD's claim and not from the road's laundered copy; it prints the count and the seqs it rewound past. Rule 2: after stamping and before anything is sent, every AUTHORED sample is checked against the per-zone blobs and the write REFUSES with exit 6, naming the sample count, the owning claim, its role and the first positions. Nothing is clamped.
AND RULE 2 IMMEDIATELY FOUND A SECOND HOLE, which is why it exists. A zone's lattice is 65 x 65 over a 64 m zone, so the BOUNDARY ROW IS SHARED and one world sample sits in two compilers -- while `Applied.sample` resolved it to `tcdata.zone_of`'s zone only. MEASURED: sample (498, 96) is `wt-south` seq 373's pad in zone (8,1); `zone_of` says (8,2), where nobody wrote it, so `foreign_at` answered None and a road was free to author a watchtower's floor. At (522, 480) zone (8,7) holds it as `tree-sth-2` seq 669's pad and zone (8,8) holds it as a road, and `zone_of` picked the road -- two compilers disagreeing about one square metre. `applied.py` now has `holders(sx, sz)`, every write whose zone lattice holds that sample, and `owners_at`/`foreign_at` go through it. Heights are unchanged: the engine renders each zone's own mesh, so `sample()` and `delta_at` still resolve by `zone_of`. This is independent of the union and predates it. S8-wtsouth-treesth re-planned after the fix authors 17 fewer samples -- 8 in tree-sth-2#669, 9 in wt-south#373 -- and its plan is clean; those 17 are in the blob that is on disk today and a re-emit now refuses rather than repeating them.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

repair_before.instrument: tools/jumpstart/roads/applied.py: every terrain_write blob for these zones decoded and unioned per sample index in FILE ORDER (later wins, which is what the live compiler holds), added to the cached generated heights, and blended bilinearly exactly as Heightmap renders the mesh. This is the surface the player is standing on right now.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

approach_grading.method: MEASURED: the live applied surface from the ledger's own blobs (union per zone in file order + generated, blended bilinearly as Heightmap renders it) at every 1 m station the road does not own, then the planned profile clamped into each claim's +/-BATTER_GRADE cone. The pad keeps every sample it owns; only the ROAD's target height moves.
approach_grading.ramp_grade_is: steeper than design, capped at BATTER_GRADE

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.
