params.datum: road profile: fitted longitudinal profile, lowest_major_walkable_surface is not applicable to a ribbon

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. Road-surface vegetation clearing is a SEPARATE op recorded by tools/jumpstart/roads/clear.py, which passes destructive=True to this same instrument and censuses each removal cylinder live in the same call
location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.
location_check.mod_free_caveat: This dump is MOD-FREE by construction (run_locscan.sh excludes BepInEx/), so it CANNOT see More_World_Locations' ~190 POI types. MEASURED: three of four live markers in GroundTruth's test zones were invisible to it. A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

params.text:
ROADCLOSE PASS. TOKEN RELEASED. Backup before the first write: world_backups/world-Ulfsland-backup-2026-09-16_13-28-04.tgz. Saved at seq 1678 with a verified postcondition (4 zone centres, 1 _TerrainCompiler each).
T1-portalhub-temple: clearing COMPLETED -- 17 further cylinders emitted (seq 1644-1655, 1657-1661), 199 more objects removed; 46 of 47 cylinders now recorded, 470 of 3,888 censused objects matched as verified-deleted, 18 clearable objects still standing inside the derived clear width (all in the six cylinders the POI/blocker gate shrank or skipped, and the batter clipped around them: 43 samples clipped beside a live placed object). Battered as a repair of seq 413 -> terrain_write seq 1666. Transverse before -> after: carriageway 1 m p50 0.320 -> 0.158, max 4.150 -> 1.485; own earthwork p95 1.419 -> 0.781, max 5.548 -> 3.626; over-grade fraction 0.1004 -> 0.0367 against 0.8613 (0.7813 batter grade + 0.08 diagonal); legacy band p50 1.365 -> 0.781, which is the design grade exactly. Longitudinal 8 m gradient 0.2407 (limit 0.781, the 38 deg slide angle); the 1 m figure beside it, a different quantity, is 1.4112. zone_ctrl 1 of 1 in all nine zones, 0 past the +/-8 m clamp, 0 below water 30.0. 37 over-grade pairs of 6,316 unexplained by a recorded clip, 10 stations, largest adjacent run 7 -- the same family as the accepted T4 (32/10/4) and T9 (14/9/4). 21 interstice rays at the T13 junction left ungraded and RECORDED (profile difference 3.15-4.53 m against 0.01-0.61 m the grade can absorb across the gap): never grade two roads into each other.
S1-portalhub-brgs2: censused 2,351 objects over 7 cells, 1 cylinder cleared, 0 clearable left inside the clear width. Battered as a repair of seq 417 -> terrain_write seq 1675: 91 paved + 65 shoulder + 26 batter samples over 2 zones, cut -1.441 fill 1.076. Carriageway 1 m p50 0.305 -> 0.134, max 1.025; own earthwork p50 0.249 p95 0.630 max 0.698 over 39 pairs, over-grade fraction 0.0 -- VERDICT pass. Walls left worst 0.760 -> 0.478 m. Longitudinal 8 m 0.4374 (limit 0.781), 1 m figure 1.75. zone_ctrl 1 of 1 in both zones, 0 past the clamp, 0 below water. THE JUNCTION CREST IS UNTOUCHED AS RECORDED: 22 samples refused beside a protected piece and a 1.5 m gap at (-315.3, 229.3) with fill -1.067 at its edge -- bridge-s2-portalhall-strait's 156 protected pieces measure worst applied delta 0.000 m in this write's own location_check, so the bridge is provably unmoved and the 0.37-0.44 m crest is left exactly as ruled.
THE WRITE-TIME PAD-FOOTPRINT GUARD IS LANDED in ledger/writer.py::Ledger._pad_footprint_check, wired into _cross_record_checks beside the zone-clobber and flatten-FORBIDDEN invariants, so it fires for every appender and not only for ribbon.py. A pad is recognised by SHAPE (pad_w/pad_d + target_y, the schema's own target_y-XOR-profile distinction) not by a role list; its footprint is pos + pad_w/2+apron x pad_d/2+apron, with the position resolved from the site's sibling records because a pad's terrain_write carries no pos at all (all 50 resolve, 0 do not); AND the ground the pad itself levelled, because stenvik-stonehouse-1 seq 272 authored 165 samples of which only 60 are inside its 11.0 x 15.0 m rectangle. PROVEN BOTH WAYS OFFLINE BEFORE ANY WRITE, on a sandbox copy of the chain: it FIRES on the no-rewind T8 re-repair fixture built from the ledger's own blobs (316 samples across 4 pads -- stenvik-beehive-1 166, stenvik-house-3 91, stenvik-stonehouse-1 39, wt-town 20 -- naming the count, the rectangle and the claim that holds each sample), and it PASSES T1's and S1's new writes at the portal hall pad, which is where the road legitimately terminates. It also PASSES 11 of the 15 landed road claims and reports 91 genuinely contested samples on the other four (T8 58, T9 17, W5 16) as pre-existing state, not as anything this pass did.
RULE 1 IS NOW AUTHORSHIP, NOT A NAME FILTER, and the name filter was wrong in the direction nobody had measured. Dropping a segment's own zone entries cures T8 and CAUSES the mirror defect: the portal hall's pad seq 801 unioned S1's carriageway forward bit-identically (sample (-300, 214) is -1.694 in both blobs), so with S1's own records dropped the hall became the first claim to hold those samples and read as their author. foreign_at then answered portal-hall#801 over the whole 30.6 m ramp, the rasteriser refused all 215 carriageway samples and stamped ZERO: the first surface a player walks off a portal was unrepairable, and no name filter can fix it because the laundered copy is under the HALL's name. applied.py::Applied.zone now composes an AUTHOR per sample -- the last claim whose value DIFFERED from what the claims before it had composed -- beside the holder, holders()/owners_at()/foreign_at()/sample() all answer by author, and nothing is dropped from the composition, so a carried copy can never become a first write. Both directions fall out of one measurement. ribbon.py's rule-2 guard and the new ledger guard were both rewritten onto it; before that, ribbon's guard refused 156 of S1's own samples to the hall at positions like (-302, 212) that are outside the hall's rectangle entirely.
T4's CLIFF, DIAGNOSED AND NOT YET REPAIRED, and the cause is one constant. APPROACH_MAX_M was 11.5 m on the stated reasoning that 'the apply clamp is +/-8 m, so the largest step the road can possibly owe a pad is 8 m, and 8/0.781 = 10.24 m of run removes it at grade'. THE PREMISE IS FALSE: the clamp bounds one terrain_write against the GENERATED height and does not bound the step between a road's profile and a pad's levelled datum, because the pad spends a clamp budget of its own in the other direction -- T4's measured residual at stenvik is -10.414 m, 2.4 m larger than the largest step the constant assumes can exist. With the run capped at 11.5 m the ramp grade saturates at BATTER_GRADE, which IS the slide limit, so the last stretch is unwalkable by construction and T4's 8 m gradient measured 0.8849. Landed: APPROACH_MIN_M 11.5 as a FLOOR, APPROACH_RUN_CAP_M 240.0 as the ceiling the function's own docstring already claimed, and ribbon.approach_reach_m deriving the run as step/design bounded by the segment's own length -- so the grade lands ON the design 8 % whenever the run is there. MEASURED offline after the change: T12 2.991 -> 0.032 m over 23 nodes (was 0.070 over 11) and T4 2.824 -> 0.656 m over 114 nodes. The T12 regression this constant was shrunk to avoid cannot recur because a claim now REQUIRES a non-zero live delta -- somebody's earthwork, not somebody's intention.
AND THE REAL T4 CAUSE IS BIGGER THAN THE RAMP, MEASURED, NOT FIXED: stenvik's keep-out in settlements/sites.yaml is pad_radius_m 100.0, a DISTRICT radius, and the rasteriser treats it as a pad. T4 therefore writes NOTHING for 293.9 m of centreline at (544.8, 809.2) and the step across that gap is -8.491 m. The foundations that must not move are the per-building site_pads (26.1, 20.3, 16.0, 11.0 m), and stenvik-house-3 at (606.5, 938.8) is 113 m from the town centre -- OUTSIDE the 100 m disc -- so roads already write inside the district and the guard that now protects the real footprints is exactly what makes doing so safe. Re-solving T4's profile alone cannot close a 294 m unwritten gap; the road has to be RASTERISED through the district, skipping only the building rectangles. That is the repair, it is one change to what pad_keepouts means, and it was not attempted tonight rather than attempted half-way.
NETWORK-WIDE, the two closing numbers, read off the ledger and applied.py rather than off any one report. TREES STILL STANDING INSIDE THE DERIVED CLEARING WIDTH: 278 per-segment records over the 13 segments whose pre-clearing censuses survive, 268 distinct ZDO ids once corridors that overlap are deduplicated -- T4 85, T5 75, S8 33, T1 18, S7 15, T13 13, T10 12, W5 11, T8 9, W10 4, T9 3, S12 0, S1 0. Every one of them is inside a cylinder the POI/blocker gate shrank or skipped, is recorded in that cylinder's skip reason, and had the batter clipped around it rather than under it. T12-wtspawn-temple and T3-temple-meadhall were cleared (26 and 28 cylinders in the chain) in a session whose census files no longer exist, so 268 is a LOWER BOUND over 13 of 15 segments and that is stated rather than rounded up. WORST TRANSVERSE 1 m STEP ANYWHERE ON THE NETWORK: 7.749 m on S7-stathub-wtnorth, unchanged by its repair; then T4 6.774, T9 6.752, T5 and T13 5.817. The worst on a CARRIAGEWAY is T4's 6.556 m, also unchanged, and correctly so -- those samples are stenvik's pad and the pad wins inside its footprint.

walkability.method: MEASURED on the APPLIED surface, not the plan: the centreline is walked at 0.5 m and each station's height is the bilinear blend of the four generated samples around it PLUS this write's bilinear delta (unwritten samples contribute zero), which is how Heightmap composes the mesh. The VERDICT gradient is taken over a 8.0 m baseline between two stations whose whole run is on written road; the 1 m figure is reported beside it and is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY -- one lattice edge -- which is why it is not the verdict. Limit is tan(38 deg), the MEASURED slide angle.

transverse.method: MEASURED: the applied surface (generated bilinear + delta_at, i.e. how Heightmap composes the mesh) sampled across the ribbon at 1 m lateral pitch every 2 m of centreline, reporting the largest adjacent-sample difference inside the carriageway, on the ground this write MODIFIED, and on untouched natural ground, separately. The verdict is the earthwork set against BATTER_GRADE plus the segment's own longitudinal grade as a diagonal allowance -- NOT a flat 0.5 m, which fails a correctly battered segment. This is the transverse quantity; walkability's gradients are the longitudinal one and cannot see a wall beside the road.
transverse.verdict_band: every adjacent 1 m pair outside the carriageway with a sample THIS WRITE wrote under it; pairs whose only written sample belongs to another claim are reported as junction_* and are that claim's to grade

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. The worst absolute delta over the disc is compared to the tolerance. Distance is a proxy for this; this is the thing itself.

location_check.destructive_claim: this terrain op emits zones_generate + terrain_write only and never objects_clear, so it cannot delete a location's ZDOs; verifiable from the ledger records for this segment. location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. Compared against the MINIMUM distance from the caller's own written samples, plus half_width_m for the caller's geometry. The declared radius is kept in the max() because 28 of 177 types carry <= 2 ZNetView children and their measured reach understates them.

A live LocationProxy sweep after zones_generate is the only complete test -- live positions for POSITION, this dump for per-type RADIUS. Clearing this check is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT.

params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.

split_of.why: SPLIT, NOT SHRUNK. The hazard is the blocker's own neighbourhood, and pulling the parent disc in CONCENTRICALLY treats it as if it were the whole disc: a blocker near the centre erases the disc, and a blocker near the rim erases the rim. MEASURED, at the exact cost of this ticket: T12's disc at (77.58,-67.58) met a generated wood house 4.71 m from its centre, shrank from 15.34 m to 3.84 m (seq 937/952), removed 4 objects and left 14 standing -- 13 of them then BURIED by this segment's own terrain write, worst 3.818 m. It recorded no skip reason because nothing was skipped; a shrink is silent. So the disc is now covered by SUB-DISCS, each a strict SUBSET of the parent (so the over-reach fraction the parent's radius encodes is preserved exactly) and each WHOLLY outside every blocker's standoff (dist(sub_centre, blocker) >= sub_radius + BLOCKER_STANDOFF_M) -- the same shape as `footprint_clear`'s rule for a POI's own extent. The per-cylinder live census in `emit` still refuses any sub-disc that turns out to hold a non-CLEARABLE prefab, so the mod-POI gate is untouched. An object no sub-disc can reach is recorded PER OBJECT with the blocker that binds it, because 'left standing' with no reason is what was reported to the operator as fixed.

delta_gate.method: MEASURED: for every location instance within 60 m of the written set, the applied height delta is evaluated on a 1 m lattice over that instance's own reach disc (reach is max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM), up to 35.77 m) by bilinear blend of the four TerrainComp samples around each probe, with unwritten samples contributing zero -- which is how Heightmap renders the ground. location_check.method: MEASURED per location TYPE: max(exteriorRadius, interiorRadius, znviewReachM) from the LocScan.cs dump, plus a 12 m margin (taste) and a 90 m extra (taste) where the generator treats the instance as load bearing -- prioritized OR centerFirst OR quantity <= 5. params.method: MEASURED live over the RCON SOCKET ONLY, PER CELL rather than per station, and with NO PREFAB LIST. The corridor is covered by DISJOINT 16 m cells on a global 16 m lattice that divides the zone grid exactly, kept where the cell square intersects clear_half(station) + 1 m of any non-bridge station. Per cell, one UNSCOPED `findObjects -near cx y cz 8` at each of FIVE y levels (-32, -16, 0, +16, +32) returns every ZDO in that box with its prefab and position -- so the census cannot be blind to a prefab nobody wrote down, including the ~190 mod POI types corridor_prefabs.json cannot name. The y stack exists because `findObjects -near` is a CUBE IN ALL THREE AXES: MEASURED, the old per-station census missed six `wood_beam_1` at the T10 spawn hall because they stand at y 84-85 and its box, centred on the road profile at 75.73 with a 7.42 m half, could not contain them. A box answering more than 18 rows is re-asked as eight sub-boxes that TILE it (half/2 at +/-half/2, 1.02 float margin), so no reply approaches the 4050-byte truncation. Deduplicated by ZDO id; `_*` engine objects are tallied separately because a removal wire can never touch them. Nothing goes through the container console: the log path died mid-census on T4 and the socket did not. Distance to the ribbon, station, clear half-width and in_clear_width are computed LOCALLY from the returned position by ribbon.lateral_and_y -- the same function that decided where the road went -- so no distance costs a call.
